article.articleHeadline: 登革熱疫情延燒 臺東出現境外移入確診首例個案 - 生活新聞 - PChome Online 新聞
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue fever outbreak continues to spread as Taitung reports its first imported confirmed case.
article.articleSummary: First imported dengue case in Taiwan's Taitung County: a man who traveled to Malaysia and the Maldives returned home and tested dengue NS1 positive on arrival at Taoyuan Airport. On Aug 8, the Taitung County Health Bureau completed case investigation and preventive measures, conducting density assessments and environmental inspections within 50 meters of the patient’s residence and related venues. As of Aug 9, Taiwan reported 119 dengue cases (7 locally acquired, 112 imported). Imported cases dominate the tally, with Southeast Asia contributing Indonesia 25, Vietnam 23, Maldives 15, Malaysia 12, Philippines 11, Cambodia 9, Thailand 6, India 6, Sri Lanka 4, and Singapore 1. Preventive guidance emphasizes wearing light-colored long-sleeved clothing, pants, shoes, and socks; applying DEET-containing repellent; regular cleaning and draining of standing water; travelers should report travel history; clinicians should perform NS1 rapid tests for suspected dengue and notify authorities. Health official Sun Guoping urges ongoing vector-control during the monsoon, reminding residents to remove standing water weekly.

triage.headline_ja: 登革熱疫情拡大、台東で境外移入による確定初例が発生
triage.triage_reason: 台湾における輸入デング熱の症例報告であり、現時点で重篤性や異常な拡大は認められないが、東南アジア各国からの輸入例が継続しているため経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 本記事は台湾（台東県）における輸入デング熱症例の監視状況を報じたものであり、感染発生国（インドネシア・ベトナム・フィリピン・タイ・インドなど）は感染経路の内訳として言及されているのみで、これら諸国自体でのアウトブレイクを主題とした記事ではないため、verified_locationsには含めない。

article.articleHeadline: Emergence of a Bundibugyo virus variant in the 2026 outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda - Nature Medicine
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Bundibugyo virus disease (BVD), caused by Bundibugyo virus (BDBV, Orthoebolavirus bundibugyoense), declared in May 2026 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) with locally transmitted cases in Uganda. This follows prior BVD outbreaks in 2007-2008 in Bundibugyo District, Uganda, and in 2012 in Isiro, DRC. Researchers generated 22 genomes from BVD samples in DRC and Uganda, forming a well-supported phylogenetic cluster distinct from lineages linked to 2007 and 2012 outbreaks, with evidence of sustained human transmission. This supports emergence of a new zoonotic spillover event rather than resurgence of previous variants. The report advocates strengthened surveillance, community engagement, Ebola treatment centers, and targeted countermeasures, plus expanded decentralized laboratory diagnostics, including pan-Orthoebolavirus assays and genomic sequencing, to limit spread and enable timely detection and control of future outbreaks.

triage.headline_ja: 2026年のコンゴ民主共和国およびウガンダにおけるアウトブレイクでのブンディブギョウイルス変異株の出現 - Nature Medicine
triage.triage_reason: エボラ関連ウイルス（ブンディブギョウウイルス）の新規ズーノーシス由来変異株によるアウトブレイクで、DRC・ウガンダ2カ国にわたる持続的ヒト-ヒト感染が確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。新規変異株による人獣共通感染症の新たなスピルオーバーであり、既存流行株とは異系統であることが遺伝学的に確認されている点が重要。

article.articleHeadline: Epidemija ebole počela mesecima pre nego što je proglašena: Više od 1.900 mrtvih, "Mi jurimo virus, a virus je ispred nas" - SZO šalje jezivo upozorenje
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola epidemic began months before it was declared: More than 1,900 dead, "We are chasing the virus, and the virus is ahead of us" - WHO sends a chilling warning.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 4,200 confirmed cases and more than 1,900 deaths, per WHO. The fastest-growing Ebola epidemic on record began in February and was officially declared on May 15; sequencing shows early cases were misattributed to malaria and typhoid. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment, and initial testing focused on the more common strains, delaying detection. Health authorities warn the virus is spreading faster than response efforts, with 60–70% of new infections among people not previously identified as contacts. Transmission occurs via bodily fluids and contaminated surfaces. The outbreak is centered in eastern Congo near borders with South Sudan, Uganda and Rwanda, in a region affected by conflict and restricted access. By comparison, the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak had about 28,000 cases and over 11,000 deaths.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行は発表の数か月前から始まっていた：死者1,900人超、「我々はウイルスを追っているが、ウイルスは我々より先を行っている」―WHOが恐ろしい警告を発する
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国東部で確認例4,200人・死者1,900人超と過去最速の拡大を見せるエボラ流行であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当し、WHOが警告を発するなど社会的関心も高いためフルRRAへ進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 発生地域にはSudan, Angola, Rwanda, Ugandaも含まれているが、記事本文では流行の中心はコンゴ民主共和国東部（南スーダン・ウガンダ・ルワンダとの国境地帯）であり、これらの国は隣接地域として言及されているのみで、実際の発生国としての記述はない。対象国リストにも該当しないため除外した。

article.articleHeadline: Gripe aviária avança em SP: Estado confirma segundo caso do ano no Ibirapuera
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Avian influenza advances in São Paulo: State confirms second case of the year in Ibirapuera Park.
article.articleSummary: Second confirmed case of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (IAAP) in São Paulo State, detected in a wild irerê (Dendrocygna viduata) found in Ibirapuera Park, São Paulo. The bird is not resident in the park, and the case is isolated with no link to commercial poultry or food-production chains. Diagnosis was confirmed by the Federal Laboratory of Agricultural Defense. No poultry establishments within 10 km of the site. Agro-defense teams will conduct epidemiological surveillance for deaths or symptomatic birds and educate residents on preventive sanitary measures. The event does not alter São Paulo’s or Brazil’s sanitary status with the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH/OIE), nor export restrictions on meat and eggs; poultry production remains intact and consumption is safe. No human infections reported; close contacts are monitored. The first case occurred July 15 in a rescued irerê near Guaíra Zoo, Barretos region, triggering surveillance within 10 km of the zoo.

triage.headline_ja: サンパウロで鳥インフルエンザが進行:イビラプエラ公園で今年2例目を州が確認
triage.triage_reason: 野鳥における単発の鳥インフルエンザ検出であり、家禽・食品供給網との関連なし、人への感染も報告されていない。WOAH衛生ステータスや輸出規制への影響もなく、社会的関心も限定的。
triage.notes: 野鳥（irerê）における孤立した検出例で、商業養鶏や人への感染は確認されていない。ブラジルのWOAH衛生ステータスや貿易には影響なし。

article.articleHeadline: 衞生防護中心：20個月大男嬰感染甲型流感 情況危殆 - 香港商報
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Centre for Health Protection: 20-month-old baby boy infected with Influenza A, in critical condition - Hong Kong Commercial Daily
article.articleSummary: Hong Kong's Centre for Health Protection reports a serious pediatric Influenza A infection in a 20-month-old boy. On August 7 he developed fever; on August 8 he was brought to a private clinic after a seizure, then admitted to Queen Elizabeth Hospital in PICU with hypotension. Lab tests confirmed Influenza A, diagnosed as influenza with septic shock; the patient remains critically ill. The initial investigation found no travel outside Hong Kong during the incubation period; one household contact recently had mild upper respiratory symptoms and tested positive for influenza by rapid antigen test, but recovered without hospitalization. Since late June, seven severe pediatric influenza cases have been recorded in Hong Kong, including one death. CHP Director notes the season remains highly active. The government has completed procurement for the 2026/27 seasonal influenza vaccination programme and is coordinating school outreach to boost uptake.

triage.headline_ja: 衛生防護中心：20カ月齢の男児がA型インフルエンザに感染、危篤状態 - 香港商報
triage.triage_reason: 香港で季節性インフルエンザによる重症小児例（PICU入院、敗血症性ショック）が報告されているが、季節的に予想される流行の一部であり異常性・国際的拡大リスクは低い。ただし7件の重症小児例と1件の死亡が続いていることから経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 香港は対象国リストに個別項目がないため、China(1814991)に統合して計上。季節性インフルエンザの活発なシーズン中の重症小児例報告であり、渡航歴なし、家庭内接触者は軽症で回復。ワクチン接種プログラムも進行中で、当局は通常のサーベイランス対応を実施している。

article.articleHeadline: Viral Marker Strategies Boost Hepatitis B Cure Prediction
article.articleSummary: Chronic hepatitis B (CHB) management advances toward a functional cure, defined as sustained loss of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg), with covalently closed circular DNA (cccDNA) persistence preventing complete eradication. A China-based team led by Prof. Qishui Ou and Prof. Zhen Xun at Fujian Medical University reviewed HBV viral markers for predicting functional cure. Published June 27, 2026 in Portal Hypertension & Cirrhosis, they find quantitative HBsAg (qHBsAg) remains the most clinically valuable single predictor, with baseline levels and early declines during Peg-IFN-α therapy informing sustained HBsAg clearance. Multimarker models incorporating additional viral markers often outperform single markers, though qHBsAg is most cost-effective in primary care settings with limited testing resources. The authors propose a framework for pretreatment stratification, monitoring response, timing NA discontinuation, and consolidating after HBsAg loss, integrating host factors and future AI/high-sensitivity assays to personalize CHB care and advance WHO elimination goals.

triage.headline_ja: ウイルスマーカー戦略がB型肝炎治癒予測を向上
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は慢性B型肝炎の治療・予測マーカーに関する研究レビューであり、アウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の緊急事態には該当しない。
triage.notes: 研究論文の紹介記事であり、アウトブレイク事案ではないため対象国の発生地域としては計上しない。

Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: দিল্লিতে লাফিয়ে বাড়ছে H1N1 সংক্রমণ, সাধারণ সর্দি নাকি সোয়াইন ফ্লু, বুঝবেন কী করে?
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In Delhi, H1N1 infections are rising rapidly; is it the common cold or swine flu, and how can you tell?
article.articleSummary: H1N1 influenza (swine flu) is described as highly contagious, with infections rising rapidly in Delhi, India. Transmission occurs via droplets from sneezing or coughing and through contact with contaminated objects. Symptoms overlap with a common viral illness and include sneezing, cough, mild fever, body aches, and runny nose, with monsoon season or seasonal changes potentially triggering these symptoms. The piece cautions that such signs should not be dismissed, given the increasing H1N1 cases in the capital. Distinguishing swine flu from a regular cold is highlighted, though no specific case counts or laboratory confirmation details are provided. The article underscores awareness of an ongoing Delhi outbreak and advises vigilance for H1N1 among symptomatic individuals during the season.

triage.headline_ja: デリーでH1N1感染が急増、風邪か豚インフルエンザか？見分け方は
triage.triage_reason: デリーでH1N1（季節性インフルエンザ）の増加が報じられているが、具体的な症例数や重症度、検査確定情報が不足しており、通常の季節的流行の範囲か判断できないため注視が必要。
triage.notes: H1N1はインドで季節性に流行する既知の疾患であり、本記事は健康啓発目的の一般的な内容で、具体的な患者数や医療機関の状況などのデータが欠如している。

article.articleHeadline: WHO: Ebolautbrottet började redan i februari
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: The Ebola outbreak began as early as February.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo began in February, months before it was publicly acknowledged in May, the World Health Organization said. WHO Africa regional director Mohamed Yakub Janabi told a press conference on Monday that sequencing showed transmission had been under way for several months prior to the formal declaration on 15 May. Some early cases were wrongly attributed to malaria and typhoid. The outbreak is described as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record. 'We are chasing the virus, the virus is ahead of us,' Janabi stated. Sequencing showed transmission had been ongoing for several months prior to the May 15 declaration.

triage.headline_ja: WHO:エボラ出血熱の流行は2月に始まっていた
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の流行がコンゴ民主共和国で確認され、史上最速の拡大とされており、公衆衛生上深刻かつ異常な事象であり、国際的拡大リスクもあるためフルRRAに進むべき。
triage.notes: 初期の症例がマラリアや腸チフスと誤診されていたことが流行の早期発見を遅らせた要因とされる。WHOは『史上最速の拡大』と表現しており、監視・対応体制の強化が急務。

article.articleHeadline: Hortolândia registra 122 casos de dengue e mantém alerta para primavera
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Hortolândia records 122 dengue cases and remains on alert for spring.
article.articleSummary: Hortolândia reported 122 dengue cases in 2026, from 2,032 notifications by the Unidade de Vigilância de Zoonoses (UVZ) of the Secretaria de Saúde, with no deaths. The figures raise spring–summer preparedness as conditions may favor Aedes aegypti. Chikungunya has 27 notifications, none confirmed; no Zika notifications were recorded. Inspectors are touring Jardim Residencial Firenze and Vila Real to remove water-holding containers that can breed mosquitoes, with Vila Real showing a July larval-density index (ADL) of 3.5. About 80% of dengue breeding sites are inside homes, underscoring the importance of interior inspections. Inspectors wear uniforms and ID badges; residents can verify actions with UVZ at (19) 3897-3312 or (19) 3897-5974. Guidance: keep yards, exteriors, pots, and containers free of standing water to curb mosquito reproduction.

triage.headline_ja: オルトランディア市、デング熱122例を記録し春に向けて警戒継続
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル一地方都市における通常のデング熱サーベイランス報告であり、死亡例なく、規模も小さく、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。
triage.notes: 地方自治体レベルの定期的な蚊媒介性感染症サーベイランス報告。死亡例なし、規模も限定的で、地域の公衆衛生対応の一環と判断される。

article.articleHeadline: L'épidémie d'Ebola sans précédent propulse la recherche de nouveaux traitements en RDC
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The unprecedented Ebola outbreak drives the search for new treatments in the DRC.
article.articleSummary: Democratic Republic of Congo faces the largest Ebola outbreak on its soil, driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus. As of 2026-08-10, 3,748 confirmed cases, 1,657 deaths, and 708 recoveries are reported, with 567 new cases and 296 deaths in the past week—the highest weekly toll since May 15. The outbreak spans 49 health zones across five provinces: Ituri (epicenter, ~90% of cases), Haut-Uele, North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tshopo. About 17,000 contacts are being followed, roughly 80% daily. Response efforts accelerate under WHO’s R&D Blueprint, with the INRB-led PARTNERS therapeutic trial enrolling in three Ituri centers and a post-exposure prophylaxis study using obeldesivir (ten days, oral) in the same area. Vaccines advance in parallel: an Oxford University/Serum Institute of India candidate began Phase 1 in the UK on July 24; a Moderna candidate starts Phase 1 in Canada; preclinical data on Ervebo seek to assess protection against Bundibugyo. WHO warns that resources remain insufficient and calls for increased funding and operational support.

triage.headline_ja: 前例のないエボラ流行がDRCでの新治療法研究を加速
triage.triage_reason: DRCで史上最大規模のエボラ（ボンディブジョ株）流行が継続し、死亡率が高く5州に拡大、WHOも資金不足を訴えるなど深刻・異常な事態でIHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 英国・カナダ・インドはワクチン/治療薬の臨床試験実施国であり、実際の感染発生国ではないためverified_locationsから除外。DRC国内5州（Ituri、Haut-Uele、North Kivu、South Kivu、Tshopo）に拡大している大規模流行で、致死率約44%と非常に高い。

article.articleHeadline: ΠΟΥ για Έμπολα: Η επιδημία στο Κονγκό είχε ξεκινήσει μήνες πριν κηρυχθεί επισήμως
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO on Ebola: The Congo Ebola outbreak had begun months before it was officially declared.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo began in February and was officially declared on May 15. The outbreak is driven by the Bundibugyo Ebola virus strain, which currently has no approved vaccines or treatments, contributing to rapid spread and delays since initial tests targeted more common Ebola types. As of the latest government data, 4,200 laboratory-confirmed cases have been reported, with more than 1,900 deaths. It is the fastest-growing Ebola epidemic on record, surpassing the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak. Transmission occurs through bodily fluids (vomit, blood, semen) and contaminated surfaces/objects (linens, clothing). Ongoing armed conflict in eastern Congo near borders with South Sudan, Uganda, and Rwanda hinders access to care and surveillance; 60-70% of new cases are outside known contact networks. WHO emphasizes intensified response amid challenging conditions.

triage.headline_ja: WHOによるエボラ出血熱に関する発表：コンゴのエボラ流行は正式発表の数ヶ月前から始まっていた
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国東部でBundibugyo株による過去最速の拡大を見せるエボラ出血熱流行が発生し、確定患者4,200人、死者1,900人超と深刻な公衆衛生被害が生じており、武力衝突により対応が困難な状況にあるためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: 発生地域にはSudan, Angola, Rwanda, Ugandaも含まれているが、記事本文の主題はコンゴ民主共和国東部での流行であり、他国は国境近接地域として言及されているのみ。対象国リストにはDRCのみ含まれる。

article.articleHeadline: El brote de ébola en el Congo se inició meses antes de su declaración oficial, revela la OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak in Congo began months before its official declaration, according to the WHO.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo ebolavirus outbreak in Bunia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, began in February, months before its official declaration on May 15. WHO sequencing confirmed the start; early cases were misdiagnosed as malaria or typhoid. Confirmed cases total about 4,200 with more than 1,900 deaths. This outbreak has no approved vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo. Initial testing focused on the more common ebolavirus type, delaying response. Response is hindered by unpaid health-worker strikes, rebel threats, community resistance, misinformation, and limited protective equipment, while a large displaced population seeks water. The outbreak is the fastest-spreading in Ebola history, surpassing the 2014–2016 West Africa outbreak (over 11,000 deaths and at least 28,000 cases); eight months to 1,000 deaths in that prior event. Transmission is via bodily fluids and contaminated surfaces; 60–70% of new cases occur outside monitored contacts, indicating alarming spread. Access to care is limited, with pregnant women avoiding clinics.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行、公式発表の数ヶ月前から始まっていたことがWHOにより明らかに
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ（ブンディブギョ型）流行は約4,200例・1,900人超の死亡と重大な公衆衛生上の影響があり、ワクチン・治療法未承認、急速な拡大、国際的拡散リスクが高くIHR基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: アンゴラは発生地域に含まれるが記事本文では言及がないため除外。ブンディブギョ型エボラは承認ワクチン・治療法がなく、史上最速拡大の流行とされる点で特に注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: WHO says Congo's fast-moving Ebola outbreak started months before it was declared
article.articleSummary: Fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record in eastern Congo began in February, months before it was declared in mid-May, according to the World Health Organization. In Bunia, Congo, sequencing by WHO indicates the outbreak’s start dates to February, with some early cases misattributed to malaria and typhoid. As of 2026-08-10, responders in eastern Congo are still racing to contain transmission. WHO Africa regional director Dr. Mohamed Yakub Janabi said laboratory sequencing confirms the outbreak’s early start. The report provides no current case or death counts. The confirmation highlights challenges in surveillance and timely outbreak recognition that can delay response, underscoring the need for rapid laboratory confirmation and vigilant reporting to curb spread in Congo.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、コンゴの急速に拡大するエボラ流行は発表の数ヶ月前から始まっていたと発表
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ東部で記録上最速の拡大を示すエボラ流行であり、初期の症例が誤診されるなど監視体制の課題が明らかになっており、公衆衛生上の深刻な影響と国際的拡大のリスクが認められる。
triage.notes: 現在の症例数・死亡者数は記事に記載なし。記録上最速の拡大とされるエボラ流行であり、初期対応の遅れが指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: Brote de ébola en el Congo empezó meses antes de declararse, dice OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in Congo began months before it was declared, says WHO.
article.articleSummary: The Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo began in February, months before it was officially declared in mid-May, according to the World Health Organization. Described as the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, the surge has stretched response teams in the east as they strive to catch up. Bunia, in the DRC, is cited as a focal area in coverage. The Associated Press report indicates authorities are scrambling to contain transmission, but the article provides no specific case or death counts. The timeline underscores a delay between initial transmission and formal declaration, which may have allowed further spread and challenged surveillance and response efforts in the outbreak region.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行、発生宣言の数ヶ月前から始まっていたとWHOが発表
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCで「記録上最速の拡大」とされ、発見・宣言の遅れによりさらなる拡大の懸念があるため、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められる。
triage.notes: 具体的な症例数・死亡者数は記事に記載なし。ただし『記録上最速の拡大』という表現から重大性が示唆される。続報でのケース数確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Bangui renforce sa prévention par la vaccination
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Bangui strengthens its prevention through vaccination.
article.articleSummary: Central African Republic conducted a preventive Ebola vaccination campaign from January to April 2026, immunizing 41,442 people across 35 health districts in seven regions with 52,010 ERVEBO doses, achieving 83.9% national coverage. Priority groups included 28,935 health professionals and frontline responders to strengthen protection of healthcare capacity against potential Ebola introduction or internal spread. No Ebola cases have been recorded in the country to date. Supported by the World Health Organization and partners, the campaign also built health-system capacity through staff training, enhanced data surveillance, community sensitization, and improved coordination among actors. The initiative addresses regional risk due to a long border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo and emphasizes proactive preparedness and community acceptance to mitigate future Ebola threats and other health emergencies.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱：バンギがワクチン接種で予防を強化
triage.triage_reason: 中央アフリカ共和国での予防的エボラワクチン接種キャンペーンの成功報告であり、同国及び近隣DRCで実際のエボラ感染例は報告されていない。
triage.notes: 記事は中央アフリカ共和国での予防的ワクチン接種キャンペーン（2026年1-4月実施、83.9%のカバレッジ達成）の報告。同国でエボラ感染例は確認されていない（'No Ebola cases have been recorded in the country to date'）。DRCとの国境に関するリスク言及はあるが、DRC国内での実際の発生については記載なし。中央アフリカ共和国は対象国リストに含まれておらず、DRCについても実際の発生国として言及されていないため、verified_locationsは空配列とした。

article.articleHeadline: Kisangani : "Ebola n'est pas une histoire, encore moins un roman"(Bourgmestre de commune de Makiso) - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Kisangani: "Ebola is not a story, let alone a novel" (Mayor of Makiso commune) - ACP
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-08-10, Kisangani in the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Tshopo Province has recorded at least one local Ebola case. Makiso commune Mayor Simon Lowawa warns Ebola is a harsh reality, not a story or novel, and urges relentless sensitization and strict adherence to barrier measures. He emphasizes that behavior change following awareness efforts will help drive out the disease and notes there is no approved treatment for the Bundibugyo Ebola strain. The report also states that experimental treatments for Ebola Zaïre are being tested against Bundibugyo. The overall message calls for ongoing public health vigilance in Kisangani and the wider Tshopo region to curb transmission. Keywords: Ebola, Kisangani, Tshopo, Bundibugyo strain, Zaïre treatment trials, public health measures.

triage.headline_ja: キサンガニ:「エボラは作り話ではない、小説などでもない」(マキソ自治体区長) - ACP
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国キサンガニでエボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株、承認済み治療法なし）の症例が確認され、公衆衛生上の重大リスクと国際的拡大の可能性があるためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ブンディブギョ株には承認済み治療法がなく、エボラ・ザイール向け実験的治療薬の試験が進行中との記載あり。感染規模の詳細（症例数、死亡数等）は不明のため、続報確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Casos de sarampo sobem para 23 em São Paulo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Measles cases rise to 23 in São Paulo.
article.articleSummary: Measles cases rise to 23 in São Paulo, Brazil. State health authorities confirmed the 23rd measles case this year on Friday, with 20 cases in the capital, 2 in São Bernardo do Campo, and 1 in Guarulhos. Most affected are infants up to 1 year old; others are adults aged 20–50. First-dose measles-containing vaccine (part of the MMR triple viral) coverage is 77.5%, second-dose 65.5%, both below the 95% target, signaling higher transmission risk. The National Multivaccination Campaign 2026 began Aug 3 and runs until Sep 1 to boost coverage, including measles vaccination. The three municipalities with confirmed cases will extend vaccination to ages 6 months through 59 years in São Paulo, Guarulhos, and São Bernardo do Campo. triage.headline_ja: サンパウロで麻疹症例が23例に増加
triage.triage_reason: 麻疹症例数は23例と限定的で重症例の報告もないが、ワクチン接種率が目標(95%)を下回り感染拡大のリスクがあるため、続報を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Campinas tem 22 bairros em alto risco de transmissão da dengue
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Campinas has 22 neighborhoods at high risk of dengue transmission.
article.articleSummary: Dengue transmission risk remains high in Campinas, Brazil, with 22 neighborhoods classified as high-risk in the 32nd Arboviroses Alert of 2026. From January 1 to August 3, 2026, Campinas registered 3,658 dengue cases. High-risk areas span multiple regions: East — Jardim Guanabara, Vila Itapura; Northwest — Conjunto Habitacional Parque da Floresta, Jardim Florence I–II, Parque da Amizade, Núcleo Residencial Três Estrelas, Jardim Nova Esperança, Jardim Campos Elíseos; North — Jardim Rosalia, Vila Reggio, Vila San Martin, Residencial Campo Florido, Vila Olímpia; Southwest — Jardim Santo Antônio, Jardim Ademar de Barros, Vila Princesa, Jardim São Cristóvão; South — Jardim Noemia, Jardim Stela, Jardim Nova Europa; Southeast — Sousas. More than 1,043,650 property inspections and 53,382 fogging actions occurred Jan 1–Jul 30, aided by drone-led searches in seven addresses: Vila Boa Vista, Vila União, Jardim Morumbi, Jardim Melina I, Parque Dom Pedro II, Jardim do Lago, Parque da Figueira. Aedes aegypti also transmits chikungunya and Zika; residents should remove standing water and verify health workers’ identification.

triage.headline_ja: カンピーナスで22地区がデング熱感染の高リスク地域に指定
triage.triage_reason: デング熱の流行は地域的に継続しているが、ブラジルでは例年見られる通常の感染症サーベイランス活動であり、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低い。地方自治体レベルでの対応が行われており、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 地方自治体（カンピーナス市）が高リスク地区を特定し、防疫活動（家屋調査・燻蒸・ドローン活用）を積極的に実施している。デング熱はブラジルで季節的に流行する疾患であり、IHR基準には該当しないが、症例数（3,658件）は一定の規模があり、地域の公衆衛生上の懸念として継続監視が望ましい。

article.articleHeadline: 刚果（金）埃博拉确诊病例超4200例，病死率达45.5%
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola confirmed cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo exceed 4,200, with a case-fatality rate of 45.5%.
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo ebolavirus Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reached 4,209 confirmed cases and 1,916 deaths, a case-fatality rate of 45.5%, as of 2026-08-10. World Health Organization notes the outbreak’s spread began earlier than publicly reported, with genomic sequencing suggesting the virus may have circulated since February, several months before the May 15 official announcement. WHO warns the outbreak is accelerating and calls for urgent strengthening of containment measures. In the affected region, response strategy has shifted from traditional close-contact tracing to door-to-door, area-wide screening to detect hidden infections. Officials warn that expanding case-finding could drive counts higher in the coming weeks.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ確定患者が4,200例を超え、致死率45.5%に達する
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCで4,209例・致死率45.5%と深刻化し、WHOが拡大加速と隠れた感染の懸念を表明しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するため。
triage.notes: WHOはウイルスが2月頃から公表前より流行していた可能性を指摘し、症例発見戦略が地域一斉スクリーニングに切り替わったことでさらなる増加が予想されるとしている。

article.articleHeadline: Kasus DBD di Kabupaten Tasikmalaya Capai 200 Orang, Satu Meninggal Dunia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue fever cases in Tasikmalaya Regency reach 200, with one death.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever cases in Tasikmalaya Regency, West Java, Indonesia, rose to 200 by July 2026, with one death. The surge occurs during the prolonged dry season, driven by standing water in rarely emptied containers that foster Aedes aegypti breeding. Affected individuals span children, adolescents, and adults, with most treated at RSUD KHZ Mushafa and under ongoing monitoring. Monthly counts from January to July 2026 were 35, 24, 31, 29, 27, 30, and 24, totaling 200. Health authorities warn that cases may rise further if household sanitation is not maintained. Symptoms prompting care include prolonged high fever. Public health measures emphasize 3M Plus (drain water storage, cover containers, dispose of waste) plus mosquito eradication (PSN) and maintaining a clean, healthy lifestyle (PHBS). Vector: Aedes aegypti. Cases confirmed positive for dengue virus; no information on imported or exported cases is provided.

triage.headline_ja: タシクマラヤ県のデング熱症例が200人に達し、1人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: デング熱は当地域で流行性の疾患であり、症例数増加と死亡が報告されているが、国際的拡大リスクや異常性は低く、通常の季節的流行の範囲内と考えられるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: デング熱はインドネシア西ジャワ州の地域的な季節性流行であり、地方当局が対応中。国際的な影響や渡航制限のリスクは低いが、乾季の長期化による媒介蚊の繁殖が懸念材料。

article.articleHeadline: Instituut voor Tropische Geneeskunde onderzoekt nieuwe ebolavariant in Congo: "We hollen de epidemie achterna" | VRT NWS Nieuws
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Institute of Tropical Medicine investigates new Ebola variant in the Congo: "We are hot on the trail of the epidemic." | VRT NWS Nieuws
article.articleSummary: Belgian researchers at the Institute for Tropical Medicine launching an extensive study to map a new Ebola variant, Bundibugyo, circulating in the Democratic Republic of Congo. In collaboration with INRB, the descriptive study involves international partners and will use a dashboard to inform frontline workers in real time about new findings. Currently, little is known about this variant; early observations suggest it is less deadly than the Zaïre variant, which can cause up to 60% mortality, with Bundibugyo around 30%. The project aims to determine transmission routes, how the virus behaves in the body, and potential health and immune-system complications. Sampling is ongoing, described as a marathon, underscoring the prolonged data collection required to understand the variant and its clinical impact.

triage.headline_ja: 熱帯医学研究所、コンゴでの新たなエボラ変異株を調査：「我々は流行の後を追いかけている」
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で新たなエボラ変異株（ブンディブギョ株）が確認・研究対象となっており、致死率30%とされる重大な公衆衛生上の懸念があり、IHR基準複数に該当するためフルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ベルギーの研究機関が主体だが、実際のエボラ流行はDRCで発生しているため、Belgiumは対象国リストに含まれず除外。新変異株の特性（致死率30%、感染経路不明）についてはさらなる情報収集が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Pequenos Guardiões contra a Dengue 💙 - Prefeitura Estância Turística Guaratinguetá
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Little Guardians Against Dengue 💙 - Guaratinguetá Tourist Town City Hall
article.articleSummary: Guaratinguetá, Brazil — The City Hall’s Municipal Health Department, in partnership with the Municipal Education Department, SAEG, and Cooperativa Amigos do Lixo, launched the 'Little Guardians Against Dengue' program at Escola Professor José Benedito Averaldo Galhardo in Pedregulho on August 4–6. Targeted at first-year elementary students, the activities educate on dengue prevention, the Aedes aegypti mosquito, risks of standing water, and the importance of recycling and proper trash disposal. The next site is Escola Professora Alcina Soares Novaes in COHAB, on August 10–13. In total, 14 municipal schools will participate, empowering students to carry learned practices home and aid in dengue control. This outreach aims to reduce dengue risk by fostering community awareness from childhood.

triage.headline_ja: デング熱に対する小さな守護者たち 💙 - グアラチンゲタ観光都市市役所
triage.triage_reason: 記事はデング熱予防に関する学校での教育啓発プログラムの紹介であり、実際の感染拡大や公衆衛生上の異常事態を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 記事は予防教育活動に関する広報記事であり、実際の感染症発生・流行を報告するものではないため対象国としてのverified_locationsは空とした。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : la majorité des décès surviennent loin des centres de soins
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: the majority of deaths occur far from treatment centers.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has caused over 1,900 deaths, with 60–70% of fatalities occurring in communities far from treatment centers. The Bundibugyo strain is involved, and there is no licensed vaccine yet. Three months after the outbreak was declared May 15 in Bunia, Ituri province, the WHO says care must be brought closer to patients to halt spread. Centralization in Bunia means long travel times and late presentations; even routes to care can fuel transmission if bodies return to villages. In Aru, two weeks with no new cases; 159 contacts identified, 121 suspects; the response extended to surrounding areas, with new facilities and outreach to avoid Bunia-based care. The WHO plans 400 beds for Ebola and 100 for other health services, plus community-based measures, such as handwashing stations at markets. If momentum improves within 2–3 months, the outlook is cautiously optimistic.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ:死亡者の大半は治療センターから遠い地域で発生
triage.triage_reason: DRCでエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）の流行が継続し、死者1,900人超、地域拡大とアクセス困難が続いており、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当するためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 3か月続くエボラ流行で死者の60-70%が治療センターから離れた地域で発生。ワクチン未承認、コミュニティベースの対策強化が進行中。Aru地域では新規例なく2週間経過との報告もあり、地域差に注意。

Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: H1N1 cases surge in Delhi: What are the warning signs and how to stay safe?
article.articleSummary: H1N1 influenza, or swine flu, is surging in Delhi, India, with 1,349 confirmed cases reported this year and no deaths so far. Health Minister Pankaj Singh says Delhi hospitals are prepared, testing is ongoing, and most patients have been treated and sent home; officials note there have been no major incidents linked to H1N1. The disease is described as a seasonal respiratory infection in India, with activity rising during the monsoon. H1N1 can cause symptoms ranging from fever, aches, chills, cough, sore throat, runny or stuffy nose, red eyes, body pains, headache, and fatigue, to diarrhea and vomiting more common in children. The incubation period is about 1 to 4 days. Transmission occurs mainly via respiratory droplets and close contact, with contamination from surfaces. Preventive measures include hand hygiene, covering coughs, avoiding close contact when unwell, staying home, and mask use in crowded settings.

triage.headline_ja: デリーでH1N1感染者が急増：警戒すべき症状と予防法は？
triage.triage_reason: デリーでH1N1（季節性インフルエンザ）の症例増加が報告されているが、死者はなく病院は対応可能な状況であり、深刻性・異常性は低い。季節性の流行として経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: 季節性インフルエンザ(H1N1)としてモンスーン期に増加が見られるが、死亡例なく医療機関の対応能力あり。国際的な拡大や渡航制限のリスクは記載なし。

article.articleHeadline: La OMS advirtió que el brote de ébola en Congo comenzó cuatro meses antes de su declaración
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The WHO warned that the Ebola outbreak in Congo began four months before its declaration.
article.articleSummary: February outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (Ituri's Bunia) was declared on May 15 by the WHO. Genomic analysis traced circulation to February; early cases were misattributed to malaria and typhoid, delaying response. By 2026-08-10, the outbreak has 4,200 confirmed cases and over 1,900 deaths, making it the largest and fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in DRC. The Bundibugyo strain has no licensed vaccine or approved specific treatment; initial testing focused on a more common variant, hindering early detection. Case fatality rate is 30–50%. Health workers protest pay arrears; supplies are scarce; access is hampered by rebel threats and poor infrastructure. About 70% of deaths occur at home, indicating surveillance gaps. The outbreak crossed into Uganda, with 20 confirmed cases, 2 deaths, and 15 imported from DRC; Uganda declared Ebola-free on 28 July. This is the 17th Ebola outbreak in DRC, surpassing the 2018–2020 epidemic (3,481 cases, 2,299 deaths).

triage.headline_ja: WHOは、コンゴのエボラ出血熱の流行が発表の4カ月前に始まっていたと警告した
triage.triage_reason: DRC史上最大・最速拡大のエボラ流行（確定4,200例、死亡1,900例超、CFR30-50%）で、ウガンダへの越境例も確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準を複数満たす重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの越境感染が報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。エボラ・ブンディブギョ株にはワクチン・治療薬が未承認であり、医療従事者の未払い賃金や物資不足、反乱勢力によるアクセス制限など対応上の課題が多数存在する。

article.articleHeadline: Pemkab Nagan Raya Gencarkan Tracing TBC Integrasi CKG bagi Warga, Diapresiasi Kemenkes
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Nagan Raya Regency Government Intensifies TB Tracing with CKG Integration for Residents, Praised by the Ministry of Health.
article.articleSummary: Tuberculosis (TB) tracing is being intensified in Nagan Raya Regency, Aceh, through integration with free health checks (CKG) for residents. A total of 26 TB-CKG outreach points will operate across Nagan Raya through December 2026, with the third site scheduled for August 11, 2026 at Desa Alue Wakie, Darul Makmur District. The effort is led by Acting Health Office head Hj Syarifah Burhani SE MSi, with P2P Safrizal SKM, and executed by Dinkes in collaboration with all Puskesmas in the regency, and with support from the Ministry of Health. In addition to TB, CKG will cover other diseases. The Ministry of Health has praised Nagan Raya, noting it is among three Aceh regencies honored for CKG due to meeting targets and robust field input.

triage.headline_ja: ナガンラヤ県政府、住民向けCKG統合による結核追跡調査を強化し、保健省から評価される
triage.triage_reason: 通常の結核対策プログラム(CKG統合による追跡強化)の実施報告であり、異常な発生や公衆衛生上の緊急性を示す内容ではない。
triage.notes: 記事は結核の日常的なサーベイランス・追跡強化プログラムの実施報告であり、アウトブレイクや異常事態を示すものではない。保健省からの表彰など行政的な取り組みが主題。

article.articleHeadline: The Silent Resistance: Rethinking Ghana's Battle Against Mosquitoes
article.articleSummary: Ghana's battle against mosquitoes amid rising malaria cases is confronted by insecticide resistance and reliance on adult sprays. As of August 10, 2026, communities widely use synthetic chemical sprays and bed nets, yet vectors adapt gradually, eroding effectiveness and signaling control failures through increasing disease burden. Rapid urbanization, poor drainage, expanding irrigation, and climate shifts expand breeding sites, intensifying the challenge. The article promotes Bacillus thuringiensis var. israelensis (Bti) as a proven, accessible larvicidal option that targets larvae in stagnant water, offering minimal cost and time and zero harm to aquatic life. Emphasizing early-stage biological larviciding reframes vector management from reactive chemical dependence to proactive source-control. Normalizing larviciding at local breeding sites—before adult mosquitoes emerge—could reduce vector populations and better protect communities from mosquito-borne diseases.

triage.headline_ja: 静かなる抵抗：ガーナの蚊との戦いを再考する
triage.triage_reason: 殺虫剤耐性やマラリア対策手法に関する論説的な記事であり、急性の公衆衛生上の異常事態や新規アウトブレイクの報告ではないため、シグナルとしての該当性は低い。
triage.notes: マラリア罹患率の増加傾向と殺虫剤耐性については言及があるが、具体的な症例数・死亡者数・急性の集団発生に関する情報はなく、防除手法（幼虫防除）を提案する解説記事の性質が強い。

article.articleHeadline: Congo's Ebola outbreak started months before it was declared, says WHO
article.articleSummary: Eastern Democratic Republic of Congo Ebola outbreak began in February, fastest-growing on record, and was officially declared on May 15. WHO regional director for Africa Mohamed Yakub Janabi said sequencing shows the outbreak started earlier, with some early cases misattributed to malaria and typhoid, noting, 'the virus is ahead of us.' As of 2026-08-10, confirmed cases reached 4,200 with over 1,900 deaths. The Bundibugyo virus causing this outbreak has no approved vaccines or treatments, complicating response efforts. Responders continue to chase transmission in the DRC amid limited medical countermeasures. Early misclassification underscores the need for rapid detection and laboratory confirmation to guide public health actions.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行、発表の数カ月前から始まっていたとWHOが発表
triage.triage_reason: DRCで承認済みワクチン・治療薬のないブンディブギョ・ウイルスによるエボラ流行が拡大し、死者数も多く、IHR基準・WPRO基準双方で複数該当するため、フルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: 確定4,200例、死亡1,900人超と致死率が非常に高く、ワクチン・治療薬未承認のブンディブギョ・ウイルス株であることが特に懸念材料。早期の誤診（マラリア・腸チフスと誤認）が流行拡大を助長した点も重要な教訓として記載されている。

article.articleHeadline: La OMS vuelve a alertar sobre la expansión del ébola en el Congo: "El 70% de la gente está muriendo en sus hogares"
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO again warns about the spread of Ebola in Congo: '70% of people are dying at home'.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ituri region continues to grow. The virus began circulating in February, four months before the outbreak was officially declared on May 15, according to WHO Africa regional director Mohamed Yakub Janabi. The delay meant the virus ran ahead of response, with faster transmission and cross-border spread to Uganda. There are no vaccines or approved treatments for this strain. Insecurity in eastern DRC due to rebel activity complicates response. About 70% of deaths occur in communities at home, not in hospitals, prompting WHO to call for greater community involvement. The outbreak is the second-largest by cases in history and the largest in the DRC by infections, surpassing the 2018–2020 outbreak (2,299 deaths, 3,481 cases).

triage.headline_ja: WHOがコンゴのエボラ拡大について再び警告：「70%の人々が自宅で死亡している」
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCで史上2番目の規模に拡大し、ウガンダへの越境感染も発生。ワクチン・治療薬不在、治安不安による対応の困難さもあり、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当する。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの越境感染が報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。ワクチン・承認された治療法がない株であることも重大な懸念点。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola à Tchomia : la population sensibilisée aux mécanismes de prévention - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Tchomia: Population educated on prevention mechanisms - ACP.
article.articleSummary: As of August 10, 2026, in Tchomia, Ituri Province, northeastern Democratic Republic of Congo, an Ebola prevention and response campaign educated the population about prevention and seeking care at the Ebola Treatment Center (CTE) in Kadjugi. Health responders urged residents to visit Kadjugi CTE promptly for medical management when symptoms appear, noting that early care improves treatment chances. Dr. Andre Tebba of the response team said the Kadjugi center also treats other health conditions and is staffed by Congolese and Ugandan physicians. He cautioned against fear and stigma surrounding the treatment center and urged people to seek timely professional care. The outreach emphasizes ongoing vigilance and community collaboration to support rapid screening of suspected cases, timely referral, and to limit the Ebola outbreak in this part of Ituri.

triage.headline_ja: トチョミアでのエボラ出血熱：住民が予防メカニズムについて教育を受ける - ACP
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イトゥリ州で進行中のエボラ出血熱流行に関する記事で、高致死率かつヒト-ヒト感染のリスクがある重大な公衆衛生事象であり、国境を接するウガンダへの拡大リスクも示唆されるため、フルリスク評価に進めるべきと判断。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ（DRC）イトゥリ州トチョミアでの予防啓発活動に関する内容。ウガンダ人医師も治療センターに勤務しているが発生地はDRC国内であり、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めない。既存のエボラ流行への対応活動である可能性が高く、続報での感染者数・地理的拡大状況の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Pedido de patente de proteína aplicada ao diagnóstico de leishmaniose visceral é submetido ao INPI
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Patent application for a protein used in the diagnosis of visceral leishmaniasis submitted to INPI.
article.articleSummary: Fiocruz submitted a patent application to INPI for a chimeric protein diagnostic for visceral leishmaniasis (LV), extending the earlier Q5 protein and its US patent. The new molecule shows diagnostic efficacy in both humans and dogs using the same antigen, addressing the urban/peri-urban reservoir role of domestic dogs for Leishmania infantum in Brazil and supporting integrated disease surveillance. Diagnostics are produced by Fiocruz Pernambuco in partnership with Bio-Manguinhos/Fiocruz; validation and quality control are conducted by Fiocruz Pernambuco, ensuring lot-to-lot reproducibility for both rapid tests and ELISA. The project is led by Osvaldo Pompílio (Fiocruz Pernambuco) with post-doctoral researcher Hemilly Silva and coordinated with Bio-Manguinhos’ Immunodiagnostic Tests Laboratory. Visceral leishmaniasis is potentially fatal and targets liver, spleen, and bone marrow; early, reliable diagnostics are central to control.

triage.headline_ja: 内臓リーシュマニア症診断用タンパク質の特許出願がINPIに提出
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は診断技術（特許出願）に関する内容であり、疾病の発生や流行、公衆衛生上の緊急性を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 記事は新規診断技術（キメラタンパク質）の特許出願に関するもので、感染症の発生・流行状況を報告する内容ではない。ブラジル・ペルナンブコ州のFiocruzによる研究開発ニュース。

article.articleHeadline: Jean Kaseya : " L'épidémie d'Ebola en RDC n'est pas sous contrôle et son extension n'est pas contenue "
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Jean Kaseya: "The Ebola outbreak in the DRC is not under control and its spread is not contained."
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is not under control and not contained, with Bunia identified as the epicenter. Jean Kaseya, director-general of Africa CDC, told Jeune Afrique after a mission to Uganda—where Ebola was brought under control—that Congo's response remains lagging behind the virus's spread. He cites systemic gaps: delays in paying response teams and widespread under-detection of cases, which impede surveillance, contact tracing, and rapid isolation. The Ugandan experience shows what can be achieved with timely funding and effective detection, while the DRC's current setup continues to struggle. The article highlights the need to address financing and detection gaps to strengthen the outbreak response.

triage.headline_ja: ジャン・カセヤ氏:「コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行は制御下になく、拡大も抑制されていない」
triage.triage_reason: Africa CDC所長がDRCのエボラ流行が制御・封じ込めできていないと明言しており、公衆衛生への深刻な影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められるためフルRRAへ進めるべき。
triage.notes: ウガンダは流行が制御下にあると記載されており対象国ではないため除外。DRC（ブニア）が主要な発生地。資金不足・検出遅延など体制上の問題が指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: Pesquisa aponta redução de 61% no número de bairros em risco de casos de dengue em Fortaleza - Contexto Notícias
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Study Finds a 61% Reduction in the Number of Neighborhoods at Risk of Dengue in Fortaleza - Contexto Notícias
article.articleSummary: Fortaleza, Brazil, records a 61% drop in neighborhoods at risk for Aedes aegypti infestation in the third LIRAa survey of 2026. Risk areas fell from 41 to 16, while 36 neighborhoods were classified as satisfactory (up from 18). The Municipal Health Secretariat (SMS) notes a marked epidemiological improvement versus the second cycle, reflecting intensified vector surveillance and control as rainfall declines after the peak rainy period. The LIRAa covers 121 neighborhoods to map dengue, Zika, and chikungunya risks and breeding sites. Fortaleza maintains year‑round vigilance and broad actions: door-to-door visits; larvicides and ultra-low-volume (ULV) insecticides; reports via 156; vector monitoring; health education and social mobilization; tire removal and cleaning drives; installation and monitoring of Larvicide Dissemination Stations (EDL); cross‑city operations with neighboring municipalities (Operação Fronteira) and METROFOR vector control in stations, tunnels, train cars and rails; and transit-terminal prevention efforts. Community participation remains essential to sustain reduced transmission risk.

triage.headline_ja: 調査によりフォルタレザでデング熱リスク地区数が61%減少と判明 - Contexto Notícias
triage.triage_reason: 記事はデング熱・ジカ熱・チクングニア熱のリスク改善（ベクター対策の成功）を報じる内容であり、公衆衛生上の懸念拡大や異常事態を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 記事はリスク改善を示す好意的な内容であり、感染拡大の兆候はない。継続的なベクターサーベイランスの一環として報告されたもの。

article.articleHeadline: Еболом у Конгу заражено више од 4.200 људи
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 4,200 people infected with Ebola in Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo: confirmed cases exceed 4,200 with 1,916 deaths as of 10 August 2026. The outbreak has spread to 53 districts across five provinces, with the Ituri region remaining the epicenter, accounting for 86.5% of all cases. WHO regional director Mohamed Janabi stated the epidemiological situation remains severely challenging and called for intensified efforts to inform the population about the importance of seeking timely medical care. He noted that 60–70% of fatalities occurred at home, underscoring the need for ongoing public education on promptly accessing medical services.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラ感染者4,200人超
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCで5州53地区に拡大し、感染者4,200人超・死者1,916人と致死率が高く、公衆衛生上深刻かつ国際的拡大リスクがあるためフルRRAへ移行すべき。
triage.notes: WHO関係者のコメントあり。60-70%の死亡が自宅で発生しており、コミュニティ対応能力に課題。継続的なモニタリングと支援が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Tshopo : plus de mille chrétiens sensibilisés contre Ebola par la Croix-Rouge - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Tshopo: More than a thousand Christians raised awareness about Ebola by the Red Cross - ACP
article.articleSummary: More than 1,000 Christians from Catholic, Protestant, Pentecostal, and independent churches in Kisangani, the capital of DRC's Tshopo Province, were sensitized about Ebola during Sunday services. The Red Cross of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Tshopo chapter, conducted sessions in the Mangobo, Makiso, and Tshopo communes as part of ongoing Ebola response activities. Trésor Kayeni said the messages emphasized barrier measures, recognizing warning signs, rapid notification, reinforced hygiene, and collaboration with health services and community relays to strengthen prevention and response. The initiative aims to boost community vigilance and public involvement in Ebola prevention. For about a month, Red Cross volunteers have been deployed in Kisangani and the Bafwasende territory to raise awareness. No Ebola case counts or laboratory confirmations are provided in the report.

triage.headline_ja: チョポ州：赤十字による1000人以上のキリスト教徒へのエボラ啓発活動
triage.triage_reason: エボラ対応活動が継続中であることを示す記事だが、新規症例数やラボ確認情報がなく、既存アウトブレイクへの啓発活動の報告に留まるため、続報を注視する。
triage.notes: 記事はキサンガニ（チョポ州）およびバフワセンデ地域における赤十字によるエボラ啓発活動を報じているが、具体的な症例数や検査確認情報は含まれていない。1ヶ月間の啓発活動が継続中であることから、既存のエボラ対応が進行中である可能性が示唆される。

article.articleHeadline: Brote de ébola en República Democrática del Congo deja 1.887 muertos y supera los 4.100 casos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo leaves 1,887 dead and surpasses 4,100 cases.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reached 4,120 confirmed cases and 1,887 deaths (case fatality rate 45.8%), with data through August 6. Of cases, 721 remain hospitalized and 810 have recovered. Contact tracing stands at 83.7%. The epidemic spans five provinces, led by Ituri (epicenter) and including North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo; Ituri accounts for 86.5% of cumulative cases. Declared May 15 in Ituri, this is the second-largest Ebola outbreak in the DRC and the fastest-growing since the epidemic began, though still below West Africa 2014–2016 totals. It is the seventeenth Ebola outbreak in the DRC, caused by Bundibugyo, with a fatality rate generally 30–50%; there is no licensed vaccine or specific treatment. Uganda reported 20 cases linked to the Congolese outbreak and was declared Ebola-free on July 28, with 15 imported cases and two deaths. Transmission occurs via direct contact with bodily fluids.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ出血熱流行、死者1,887人、感染者4,100人超に
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で発生した大規模エボラ流行（症例4,120件、死者1,887人、致死率45.8%）で、5州に拡大し隣国ウガンダへの伝播も確認されており、IHR基準・WPRO基準共に複数該当する。
triage.notes: ウガンダでも輸入例（20例、死者2名）が確認されているが、対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。DRCにおける17回目のエボラ流行で、史上2番目に大きく、最も急速に拡大している流行とされる。ワクチンや特効薬は未承認。

article.articleHeadline: L'Institut de médecine tropicale d'Anvers étudie la réponse immunitaire au nouveau variant de l'Ebola au Congo | VRT NWS: le site d'information de référence
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Antwerp Institute of Tropical Medicine studies the immune response to the new Ebola variant in Congo | VRT NWS: the reference news site
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease (EVD) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is in its 17th outbreak, declared in May, starting in Ituri and spreading to North Kivu. To date, 4,053 cases and 1,850 deaths have been reported. Laurent Liesenborghs of the Antwerp Institute of Tropical Medicine (ITM) notes the virus likely circulated as early as January. ITM, which has supported clinical trials of existing therapeutics to reduce fatalities, has launched a new descriptive study focusing on the immune response to the virus’s new variant, conducted with multiple international partners. The study will observe how the new variant behaves in the body and examine potential health and immune-system complications.

triage.notes: 本記事はベルギー・アントワープの研究機関が新変異株の免疫応答を研究しているという続報だが、発生地はDRC（Ituri、North Kivu）であり、ベルギーは研究拠点に過ぎないため verified_locations には含めない。既に5月に発生宣言済みの大規模流行であり、フルRRAでの状況確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola na RD Congo: Surto pode ter começado meses antes do diagnóstico oficial
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in DR Congo: The outbreak may have begun months before the official diagnosis.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo may have begun about three months before the official announcement, prompting urgent strategy changes after genetic sequencing. WHO Africa regional director Mohamed Yakub Janabi visited Bunia, the epicenter. By Aug 7, authorities reported 4,209 confirmed cases and 1,916 deaths across Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uele, and Tshopo. It is DR Congo’s 17th outbreak and the second largest globally after 2014-2016 West Africa. Early infections may have been misdiagnosed as malaria or typhoid, delaying containment. Mortality outside treatment centers is high: 60-70% occur at home, with response teams identifying about one third of cases. Priorities include mobilizing transport networks (roughly half of deaths linked to transport), directing patients to treatment centers, and expanding facilities with 400 Ebola beds plus 100 general beds. Handwashing points at transit hubs, media outreach, and Ervebo vaccine trials; possible cross-protection against Bundibugyo is under investigation. Emphasis on community engagement, rapid detection, and decentralization over 8-12 weeks.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱：流行は公式診断の数ヵ月前に始まっていた可能性
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の大規模流行（確定4,209例、死亡1,916例）で、西アフリカ流行に次ぐ世界2番目の規模。誤診による対応遅延、複数州への拡大、国際的な公衆衛生上の重大な懸念があり、フルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: WHOアフリカ地域事務局長が現地視察を行い、国際的な対応強化（ワクチン試験、治療センター拡充等）が進行中。マラリアや腸チフスとの誤診により流行開始が数ヵ月遅れて発覚した点が特に異常性を示す。アンゴラは発生地域に含まれるが記事本文で言及なく除外。

H9N2 has human cases in China; H5N1 detected in Australian birds. Salmonella linked to jalapeños spread to 27 states; invasive E. coli shows rising drug resistance. article.articleHeadline: Three migrant workers test positive for malaria in Anavilasam; preventive measures intensified
article.articleSummary: Three migrant workers tested positive for malaria in the Anavilasam area of Idukki district, a cardamom plantation region near Kumily. Infections were detected during targeted screening of migrant laborers; patients received medication and follow-up care. Health authorities conducted contact smears, mass blood smears, and Indoor Residual Spraying (IRS) in the affected area. A panchayat meeting chaired by Rejimoal Shiby outlined intensified preventive measures, including mandatory blood testing for all workers employed by plantation owners, establishments, labor contractors, and accommodation providers in the panchayat. Incoming workers from other states will be screened for malaria and filariasis within three days of arrival and must pass a Primary Health Centre check-up with a fitness certificate proving malaria-free status before starting work. Establishments must submit worker details to Ward Health and Sanitation Committees; legal action under Public Health Act, 2023 may be taken against those enabling disease spread.

article.articleHeadline: Vigilância em Saúde reforça orientações após identificação de morcegos com raiva
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Public Health Surveillance reinforces guidelines following identification of bats with rabies.
article.articleSummary: Rabies detected in bats in Porto Alegre, Brazil. Through July this year, the Núcleo de Antropozoonoses collected 233 bats, with 11 testing positive for rabies. Sampling covered neighborhoods including Rubem Berta, Belém Novo, Tristeza, Restinga, Santana, Higienópolis, São João, Menino Deus, Vila Nova, Azenha and Cidade Baixa. In 2025, 11 of 347 bats were positive, up from 2024 (10/283). Although case counts were stable, surveillance intensified with more animals analyzed, indicating viral circulation across city regions and the need for ongoing vigilance and preventive actions. What to do: a bat that flies away indoors is likely healthy—open windows and turn off lights to encourage it out. If it remains or is found outdoors, avoid touching and contact Vigilância em Saúde for collection at (51) 3289-2450 or WhatsApp; after-hours, call 156. If exposed, wash the area with soap and water and seek care for evaluation and possible vaccination or serum. Pets should be revaccinated after exposure; bats are protected by law but contribute to ecosystems via insect control (Aedes aegypti) and pollination.

article.articleHeadline: WHO "민주콩고 에볼라 발병, 공식 선언 3개월 전 시작"
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO "Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo began three months before the official declaration"
article.articleSummary: February marked the start of an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, three months before the official declaration on May 15. Genomic analysis cited by WHO (Dr. Mohamed Yacoub Zanabi) indicates early transmission, with initial cases misdiagnosed as malaria or typhoid. As of August 7, 4,209 confirmed cases and 1,916 deaths have been reported, a case fatality rate of 45.5%. WHO and Africa CDC warn the true burden is larger, with over 70% of new infections in individuals not on contact lists and 60–70% dying at home rather than in care facilities. Contact tracing is shifting to door-to-door case finding in outbreak zones, reflecting widespread community transmission and security challenges in armed areas; officials warn cases may rise faster in coming weeks. The virus is Bundibugyo ebolavirus, not the Zaire species; authorities plan mutation surveillance. Key obstacles include armed conflict, healthcare worker strikes, distrust, and misinformation.

triage.headline_ja: WHO「コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ流行、公式発表の3か月前から始まっていた」

article.articleHeadline: Seu pet pode transmitir leishmaniose para você? Entenda | A TARDE
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Can your pet transmit leishmaniasis to you? Find out | A TARDE.
article.articleSummary: Leishmaniasis is caused by Leishmania parasites and transmitted by female sandflies. Dogs are major urban reservoirs, but transmission to humans is not direct; infection occurs via sandfly bites in areas with active vectors. Humans are accidental hosts, with low parasite burden on the skin, making human-to-vector transmission rare. In pets, dermatologic signs include alopecia around the eyes and ears, scaling, non-healing wounds, and ulcers, with possible onychogryphosis, lymphadenopathy, weight loss, apathy, and renal failure. In humans, visceral leishmaniasis (fever, hepatosplenomegaly, anemia, weakness) and tegumentary leishmaniasis (painless skin lesions; mucosal involvement) occur. Treatments differ: pets receive symptomatic relief and reduced parasite load but not complete cure, requiring ongoing veterinary care and repellents; humans are treated with antileishmanial drugs through public health systems. Untreated visceral disease can be fatal in ~90% of cases. Aug 10 is noted as National Day of Combat and Control of Leishmaniasis, with prevention focused on vector control and environmental hygiene.

article.articleHeadline: ΠΟΥ για Έμπολα: Η επιδημία στο Κονγκό είχε ξεκινήσει μήνες πριν κηρυχθεί επισήμως
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO on Ebola: The outbreak in Congo had begun months before it was officially declared.
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo began in February 2026 and was officially declared on May 15, 2026, per WHO. Genomic analysis shows the outbreak started months earlier; some early cases were misattributed to malaria and typhoid. As of government data, 4,200 confirmed Ebola cases and over 1,900 deaths have occurred. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, a rare strain with no approved vaccines or therapies. Initial testing targeted the more common Ebola type, delaying detection. Conditions are extremely challenging: unpaid health workers have held strikes, armed groups threaten communities, mistrust and misinformation circulate, and responders must travel rough dirt roads with PPE shortages. Large numbers of displaced people lack safe water for handwashing. Authorities warn that 60–70% of new infections are not among monitored contacts, and spread is advancing at a worrying pace, with some new cases doubling in hotspots.

article.articleHeadline: Cara Usir Lalat agar Tak Bertelur di Makanan, Cegah Risiko Penyakit
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: How to Keep Flies from Laying Eggs in Food, Prevent the Risk of Disease
article.articleSummary: Houseflies can contaminate food with microbes and potentially lay eggs, raising disease risk. The article notes intestinal myiasis as a possible, though rare, outcome when fly larvae develop in the digestive tract after ingestion of contaminated food. Flies carry bacteria from waste, animal carcasses, or spoiled food, making hygiene crucial. If a fly only lands briefly on food, the contamination risk is lower; longer contact increases microbial transfer. Practical, non-chemical methods to repel or trap flies include: apple cider vinegar traps with sugar and dish soap; using jars of rotting fruit with perforated lids; planting aromas flies dislike (basil, mint, lavender, cloves, cinnamon) or using essential oils, diffusers, or scented candles; and simple candle traps placed over shallow water. Flies do not have teeth and liquefy foods, so surface contamination and microbial transfer are the main concern. Keep food covered to prevent eggs or microbes from reaching food.

The strategy aims to uncover hidden infections and accelerate isolation and care. The World Health Organization has called for a change in response, with greater emphasis on community-level work and rapid case finding. The article notes escalating transmission and a broadened operational approach by health authorities; no exact case totals are provided in the summary. Report date: 2026-08-10.

article.articleHeadline: As the Ebola outbreak spreads in Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), International Rescue Committee (IRC) trains community leaders to strengthen early detection and combat misinformation
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) continues to spread, with more than 4,200 reported cases and nearly 2,000 deaths. IRC scales up community engagement in Ituri province by training local leaders and volunteers to raise awareness, counter misinformation, support early detection, and gather community concerns. Training spans 15 health areas in Bunia, Rwampara and Nyankunde, plus six sessions in Goma; after training, volunteers conduct door-to-door sessions and small discussions, collecting feedback and monitoring rumors. The outbreak’s pace has surpassed the total of the 2018–2020 outbreak in less than three months. IRC aims to strengthen infection prevention and control, surveillance, and frontline health worker support, with potential expansion into Beni and Butembo in North Kivu. Outreach targets religious institutions, schools, youth networks, women's groups, and the transport sector.

article.articleHeadline: Gripe aviária: ave silvestre é diagnosticada com a doença no Parque do Ibirapuera
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Avian influenza: wild bird diagnosed with the disease at Ibirapuera Park.
article.articleSummary: Avian influenza confirmed in a wild bird (irerê species) at Ibirapuera Park, South Zone, São Paulo. Diagnosis by the Federal Laboratory of Agricultural Defense after isolation and sampling. This is an isolated incident in a free-living wild bird with no link to commercial poultry farms or the food-production chain. No commercial poultry operations within 10 km of the park; sanitary monitoring will cover the surrounding area to detect signs or mortality in other birds and to inform visitors and residents. The incident does not alter the state or national sanitary status and does not trigger embargoes on meat or egg exports; poultry meat and eggs remain safe for consumption. The State Health Secretariat is operating a contingency plan and monitoring involved professionals; as of 2026-08-10, no human cases have been reported in São Paulo.

article.articleHeadline: DRC's Ebola outbreak began months before it was officially declared, says WHO
article.articleSummary: DRC's Ebola outbreak, the fastest-growing on record, began in February and was formally declared on May 15, with sequencing showing early cases misattributed to malaria and typhoid. Confirmed cases total about 4,200 with at least 1,900 deaths (government figures). The outbreak involves Bundibugyo Ebola virus, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments. Ebola transmission occurs via contact with bodily fluids and contaminated surfaces. Early testing focused on the Zaire strain. WHO warns cases are spreading faster, with doubling in some hotspots. Responders operate under difficult conditions: unpaid health workers striking, rebel threats, misinformation, PPE shortages, and a large displaced population lacking reliable handwashing water. The WHO-advocated full-scale human trials of Ervebo, the licensed Zaire vaccine, which may offer some protection against Bundibugyo; two Bundibugyo vaccines are in early trials, another candidate in development. Context notes the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak for comparison.

article.articleHeadline: WHO says Congo's fast-moving Ebola outbreak started months before it was declared
article.articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak has 4,200 confirmed cases and over 1,900 deaths. Declared May 15, 2026, the Bundibugyo virus has no approved vaccines or treatments, and early testing focused on the common Ebola strain, delaying response. The outbreak unfolds under severe constraints: unpaid health workers striking, rebel threats, misinformation, PPE shortages, and a large displaced population with unreliable water sources. Health teams travel remote unpaved roads as access to care erodes; fear leads pregnant women to avoid clinics. WHO says new cases are doubling in hotspots, with 60–70% of cases outside monitored contacts, signaling rapid spread. The region borders South Sudan, Uganda, and Rwanda, complicating containment. By comparison, the 2014–2016 West Africa epidemic killed over 11,000 people and had at least 28,000 cases; this outbreak is spreading faster in deaths than others.

article.articleHeadline: Congo-Kinshasa: L'administrateur de Lubero appelle à collaborer avec les équipes de riposte contre Ebola après la confirmation d'un premier cas
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo-Kinshasa: The Lubero administrator urges collaboration with Ebola outbreak response teams after the confirmation of a first case.
article.articleSummary: In Nord-Kivu's Lubero territory, Democratic Republic of Congo, the territorial administrator Colonel Alain Kiwewa confirmed a first Ebola case in the Lubero health zone, marking Lubero as the third health zone affected after Masereka and Musienene. Kiwewa urged residents to cooperate with outbreak response teams and seek care promptly at health facilities or Ebola treatment centers when symptoms appear. He stressed that the disease is real and should not be minimized, countering claims that Ebola is a myth. He cited recoveries already reported in Musienene and Masereka to reassure communities. The administrator called for rapid reporting of suspected cases and for communities to avoid behaviors that could spread the virus, promising treatment access and testing as needed. Ongoing effort: collaboration between residents and response teams to control transmission.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国:ルベロ行政官、エボラ第1例確認後、対応チームとの協力を要請
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRC北キブ州で新たな保健地区（ルベロ）に拡大し、既に複数地区で感染が確認されているため、国際的拡大リスクと公衆衛生への影響が大きく、フルRRAが必要と判断。
triage.notes: エボラは既に複数の保健地区（Masereka, Musienene, Lubero）に拡大しており、地域当局が住民の協力と早期報告を呼びかけている。感染拡大の継続が懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: 20個月大男嬰感染甲型流感併發敗血性休克 情況危殆留醫深切治療部 - 星島日報
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A 20-month-old boy with Influenza A infection complicated by septic shock; in critical condition; admitted to the Intensive Care Unit.
article.articleSummary: A 20-month-old boy in Hong Kong is in critical condition with Influenza A infection complicated by septic shock, currently in the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit at Queen Elizabeth Hospital. Reported by the Centre for Health Protection on 10 August 2026, the child had not received the 2025/26 seasonal influenza vaccine and had no travel during the incubation period. A household contact recently had upper respiratory symptoms and tested positive for influenza but recovered with mild illness. The onset occurred on 7 August with fever and a convulsive episode after a clinic visit, followed by transfer to hospital; respiratory tract testing confirmed Influenza A with septic shock. CHP will continue investigation and urges vaccination and adherence to personal and environmental hygiene to prevent influenza and other respiratory diseases.

triage.headline_ja: 20か月の男児がA型インフルエンザに感染し敗血性ショックを併発、重篤な状態でICUに入院
triage.triage_reason: 季節性インフルエンザの単発重症小児例であり、家庭内接触者は軽症で回復。異常性・国際的拡大リスクは低く、通常のサーベイランス範囲内の事例。
triage.notes: 香港特別行政区の事例だが、対象国リストのルールに基づきChina(1814991)に含めた。個別の重症小児例であり、季節性インフルエンザの通常の流行状況の範囲内と考えられる。

article.articleHeadline: La OMS afirma que el rápido brote de ébola en el Congo comenzó meses antes de que fuera declarado
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The WHO says that the rapid Ebola outbreak in Congo began months before it was declared.
article.articleSummary: February start; the rapid Congo Ebola outbreak, declared May 15, has reached 4,200 confirmed cases and over 1,900 deaths. Genetic sequencing indicates the outbreak began months earlier; some early cases were misattributed to malaria and typhoid. It is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments, and initial tests targeted the more common Ebola type, delaying recognition. The response unfolds in conflict-affected eastern Congo near South Sudan, Uganda and Rwanda, with remote roads, unpaid health workers on strike, rebel threats, misinformation, PPE shortages, and displaced populations lacking reliable water. Transmission is via bodily fluids and contaminated surfaces; new cases are doubling in places and 60–70% occur outside monitored contacts, signaling an alarming spread. By contrast, the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak caused >11,000 deaths and took about eight months to reach 1,000 deaths. Public health efforts face substantial access and security challenges.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、コンゴのエボラ流行は発表の数ヶ月前から始まっていたと発表
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でBundibugyoエボラウイルスによる大規模流行（確定4,200例、死亡1,900例超）が発生し、ワクチン・治療薬未承認、紛争地域でのアクセス制限、監視外での感染拡大など複数の重大リスクが確認されるため。
triage.notes: 発生地域にはスーダン・アンゴラ・ルワンダ・ウガンダも含まれるが、記事本文では感染拡大の主体はコンゴ民主共和国東部であり、他国は近接する国境地域として言及されているのみで実際の発生確認はない。ワクチン・治療薬がないBundibugyo種であることが特に懸念される。

diseases.name: Human Infection with Swine Influenza A H1N1

article.articleHeadline: H1N1 cases in Delhi : What are the symptoms, prevention tips as cases jump 6-fold from last year
article.articleSummary: Delhi records 1,344 H1N1 influenza cases this season, up from 229 in the same period last year, a near sixfold rise. H1N1 should not be dismissed as routine flu, as it can progress to serious illness in vulnerable groups. High-risk individuals include older adults, pregnant women, young children, people with diabetes, and those with chronic heart or lung diseases; immunocompromised people are also at greater risk. Common symptoms mirror seasonal flu: fever, cough, sore throat, runny or congested nose, fatigue, body aches, and loss of appetite, with shortness of breath possible. GI symptoms (nausea, vomiting, diarrhea) are more common in children. Antibiotics do not treat the virus; antivirals may be considered for severe illness or those at higher risk. Vaccination and basic precautions—hand hygiene, covering coughs/sneezes, avoiding sick contacts, and staying home when unwell—remain key to reducing severe outcomes.

triage.headline_ja: デリーでH1N1感染例が急増：前年比6倍、症状と予防のポイントとは
triage.triage_reason: デリーでH1N1季節性インフルエンザの症例が前年比6倍に増加しているが、季節性インフルエンザの一種であり新規性・異常性は限定的。続報を注視する必要がある。
triage.notes: H1N1は既知の季節性インフルエンザであり、症例数増加は報告されているが重症度・死亡率に関する具体的データは記事に記載なし。インド国内の公衆衛生対応で管理可能と見られる。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC: la situation "n'est pas bonne", plus de moitié de décès surviennent hors des hôpitaux, alerte l'OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: the situation "is not good", more than half of the deaths occur outside hospitals, WHO warns.
article.articleSummary: Three months after the Ebola outbreak was officially declared in the Democratic Republic of Congo, nearly 2,000 people have died and about 4,000 have been infected. The WHO Africa regional director Mohamed Janabi warns that 60–70% of deaths occur in communities, emphasizing the need to inform the public to seek medical care promptly. The Ebola Bundibugyo virus shows a case fatality rate of 45.5% based on latest data as of August 7, reported by the Congolese Ministry of Communication and Media. In five affected provinces, 4,209 confirmed cases have been recorded, with 1,916 deaths and 828 recoveries. The body of a person who has died of Ebola remains highly contagious for several days, underlining ongoing transmission risks even after death.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱：状況は「良くない」、死亡の半数以上が病院外で発生とWHOが警告
triage.triage_reason: 致死率45.5%、感染者4,000人超・死者2,000人近くという大規模流行が継続し、WHOが公式に警告している深刻な公衆衛生事象であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当する。
triage.notes: WHOアフリカ地域局長が公式に警戒を発信しており、地域内で多数の死亡が病院外で発生していることから地域内拡大・院内感染対策の脆弱性が示唆される。フルRRAへの移行が適切。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : 4 294 cas confirmés et 1 960 décès, l'Ituri reste l'épicentre - LePotentiel
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: 4,294 confirmed cases and 1,960 deaths, Ituri remains the epicenter - Le Potentiel
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo persists: as of 8 August 2026, 4,294 laboratory-confirmed cases and 1,960 deaths (case fatality 45.6%). Transmission remains active in three provinces, notably Ituri, which remains the epicenter. The outbreak response spans five provinces: Haut-Uélé, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tshopo. Overall, the epidemic covers 53 health zones (out of 140) and 246 health areas. Health authorities continue surveillance and case management in affected territories. Ituri, North Kivu and Haut-Uele still reporting transmission, while South Kivu shows improvement with 73 days without a new confirmed case. As of 8 August 2026, 722 patients are in isolation or hospital, and 849 have recovered since outbreak start. Contact tracing stands at 84.6%, enabling rapid identification of exposed individuals to reduce secondary transmission.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱：確認症例4,294人、死者1,960人、イトゥリが依然震源地
triage.triage_reason: 致死率45.6%の大規模エボラ流行が5州・53保健地区に及び継続中であり、深刻な公衆衛生上の影響とヒト-ヒト感染リスクを有するためフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: 感染は現時点でDRC国内5州に限定されており国境を越えた拡大の報告はないが、大規模かつ長期化している流行であるため継続的な監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola, strage in Congo: sale a 1.960 il numero dei morti. È la seconda epidemia più grave di sempre nel Paese
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in Congo: death toll rises to 1,960. It is the second-deadliest outbreak in the country.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is driven by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, with 4,294 confirmed cases and 1,960 deaths as of August 8, a 45.6% fatality rate. About 722 patients remain hospitalized or in isolation, 849 have recovered, and contact tracing has reached 84.6%. The virus is active in five provinces, led by Ituri (the epicenter), with transmission also in North Kivu, Haut-Uélé, and Tshopo; South Kivu reports no new cases for 73 days, suggesting containment there. The outbreak began May 15; the first case was a Bunia nurse who died April 24 from fever, hemorrhage and vomiting, but early tests targeting Zaire delayed recognition. There are no approved vaccines or therapies for Bundibugyo ebolavirus; Ervebo is ineffective against this strain. WHO declared a PHEIC; MSF opened a treatment center in Ituri, and CEPI is funding candidate vaccines and trials. Isolated Ugandan cases have not sparked further spread.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱大流行：死者数1,960人に増加。同国史上2番目に深刻な流行
triage.triage_reason: PHEIC宣言済みでワクチン・治療薬未承認の致死率45.6%のエボラ流行が拡大しており、ウガンダへの越境例も報告されているためフルRRAへの移行が必要。
triage.notes: Bundibugyoエボラウイルス株によりEnvebo等既存ワクチンが無効。ウガンダでの孤立例は今回の対象国リストに含まれないため除外。WHOはPHEICを宣言済みで国際支援（MSF、CEPI）が既に動いている。

article.articleHeadline: DRC: बच्चों पर इबोला का बढ़ता कहर, नए टीके से उम्मीद
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: Ebola's rising toll on children, hope from a new vaccine.
article.articleSummary: Eastern Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ituri province faces an Ebola outbreak with over 300 child deaths; UNICEF notes the outbreak began mid-May, with children making up about a quarter of confirmed cases but about one-third of deaths. Ituri has about 1 million displaced, roughly 80% women and children, and health services have been severely disrupted, with use dropping by over 40% in the worst-affected areas. Pregnant women are at heightened risk: obstetric complications kill about six women weekly, and Ebola during pregnancy almost always results in fetal loss. Community outreach by ~13,000 health workers (with Africa CDC, UNICEF, WHO) has informed more than 2.4 million people and visited over 500,000 households. Separately, WHO experts urge testing Ervebo—the Ebola Zaire vaccine—in controlled trials against Bundibugyo; no Bundibugyo-specific vaccine exists, and Bundibugyo outbreak was declared a PHEIC on 16 May.

triage.headline_ja: DRC:子どもへのエボラの被害拡大、新ワクチンに期待
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国イトゥリ州でエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行が続き、子ども300人以上死亡、PHEIC宣言済みであり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナル。
triage.notes: ブンディブギョ株によるエボラ流行がPHEICと宣言されており、既存ワクチン(Ervebo)は主にザイール株用のため、有効性評価のための臨床試験実施をWHO専門家が提言している。子どもと妊婦への影響が特に深刻。

article.articleHeadline: Global TB Fight Stalls Despite Modest Decline in Cases
article.articleSummary: Tuberculosis (TB) remains the world’s leading infectious killer. In 2024, an estimated 10.7 million people developed TB, including about 620,000 living with HIV, and TB caused roughly 1.23 million deaths, with around 150,000 among people with HIV. Global incidence fell 1% from 2023 to 2024 but remains well above pre-pandemic levels and off the pace to meet WHO End TB targets. Case detection reached 8.3 million notified (78% of estimated burden), aided by rapid molecular diagnostics, yet prevalence surveys show many bacteriologically confirmed but asymptomatic infections that continue transmission. Drug-resistant TB remains a major hurdle: 390,000 MDR/RR-TB cases in 2024, only 42% started treatment; 71% treatment success. 5.3 million people received preventive therapy; 58% of eligible people living with HIV, and 25% of eligible household contacts. Thirty high-burden countries accounted for 87% of cases, led by India, Indonesia, Philippines, China, Pakistan, Nigeria, DRC, and Bangladesh. Funding at 27% of targets.

triage.headline_ja: 世界のTB対策、症例数はわずかに減少するも停滞
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は結核(TB)に関する世界的な年次動向報告であり、特定の急性発生事象やアウトブレイクを示すものではないため、シグナルとしての緊急性は低い。
triage.notes: 本記事はWHOのグローバルTB報告に基づく年次統計・動向のまとめであり、単一国での急性アウトブレイクではないため、通常のEBSトリアージ対象外と判断。継続的なモニタリング対象としては意義があるが、即時のRRA実施は不要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : la majorité des décès surviennent loin des centres de soins
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: the majority of deaths occur far from care centers.
article.articleSummary: Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo has caused over 1,900 deaths, with 60–70% occurring in communities far from treatment centers, according to the World Health Organization. In Bunia, eastern DRC, patients often reach facilities too late due to distance and limited nearby care, with long travel times and poor initial treatment increasing mortality and transmission. WHO aims to decentralize care by establishing new facilities outside Bunia. In Aru, this approach already yields results: no new Ebola cases in two weeks after monitoring 159 contacts.
